Each failing row now prints one sentence naming its next step, and the facts it used to print as JSON are in the new `detail` field of `fgos doctor --json` (rows are `{id, description, passed, message, detail?}`). One doctor run reads the repository with 4 `inspectGit` calls instead of 7 (5 instead of 8 when `eventStore.remote` is not `origin`).

+- A terminal layout limit below the measured floor (`terminal.layout.minCols` under 40 or `minRows` under 8) is now refused by the terminal-control core itself, with the code `terminal-config-below-floor` naming key, value and floor, instead of running; `fgos doctor` prints that refusal in `terminal-control`. +- `/fgOS:terminal` and `/fgOS:terminal-close` no longer carry their own pane-ownership script: the terminal-control `attach` itself refuses, as `pane-not-owned`, a pane whose shell is not the caller or one of its ancestors (read from the OS, never from the request), also when the key is already bound to the pane, so a dispatch anchor pane that the dispatching process does not run in is now ignored instead of joined. On Windows only a pane whose shell is the caller itself passes (Linux and macOS read the parent chain). The doctor's anchor-pane and executor-kind rows and the worker-session socket lookup now ask the terminal-control route (`capabilities` answers `anchorPane`, `agentKinds`, `integrations` and `endpoint.socketPath`), so the driver is the only code that runs herdr's pane commands or knows its socket layout.
+- `fgos doctor` no longer closes expired retained terminal panes: the `terminal-allocations` check reports them with the pane id so a person closes them, and the allocation scan answers every finding with its `paneId`.
+- A terminal allocation, launch-requested or release marker whose directory sync failed after it was written is now answered `unknown` (`allocation-install-unproven`, the file stays as evidence) instead of success; a pane's foreground is judged closable only when the launched process still has its recorded pid, start time and boot, and an empty foreground list keeps the pane; herdr commands inherit no descriptor above 1023 and are awaited on the child's exit instead of a 1 ms poll.
+- Identity reads `PI_SESSION_ID`, which pi and omp export to their tools, as a writer id (after `CODEX_THREAD_ID`), so a pi or omp session and the tools it runs get one stable handle instead of a pid id. The handle's CLI part is `omp` or `pi`, read from the process ancestry (the nearest ancestor named `omp` or `pi`, else `pi`), never from env. A launched worker no longer inherits `PI_SESSION_ID` or `PI_SESSION_FILE`. `session_for` takes a `head_pid`.
+- `fgos identity resolve` also takes a full session id (`<machine-id>/<local id>`): of this machine it returns the exact live entry, otherwise it exits 65 with `not-found` (an id of another machine names that cross-machine resolution waits for the shared directory). The Identity library gains `session_for` and `register_writer` so a hook that gets the session id from its payload (Codex hooks have no `CODEX_THREAD_ID` in their env) registers the right session from the key and the head pid, refused `invalid-writer-key` or `head-not-live` when they do not hold.
+- The gateway, the host runtime's external-process provider manifests and the observe metrics harness now read YAML through the new Rust YAML Document crate instead of `serde_yaml`, which is unmaintained and carried advisory RUSTSEC-2024-0449. Every YAML file in this repository reads to the same value as before; a file with a duplicate key, an unknown tag or a value over the size and depth bounds is refused by a named rule with its line and column, and the error never quotes the file.
+- `/fgOS:terminal` labels and keys the caller's pane with the fgOS writer id again when `FGOS_SESSION_ID` is unset: the skill asks the activated host (`fgos identity`) instead of importing the checkout's Node facade, which refuses since the checkout channel stopped serving identity verbs, so the `fg.ssid` label segment had silently gone missing.
+- `fgos identity session --register [--role lead:<LANE> [--take]]` records this session in the machine's local directory (`<state root>/identity/sessions/`), and `fgos identity resolve <handle|lead:LANE>` returns exactly one live session of it, or exits 65 with `not-found` or `ambiguous` and the candidates; `fgos identity list [--project] [--prune]` shows the sessions the machine knows. Nothing registers on its own (the bare verb, plain `session`, hooks and workers add no entries); liveness is judged from the agent's terminal-holding head process, dead entries go on the next write, a second live session with the same handle or a role held by another live session is refused (`--take` moves a role), and a full directory (512) is emptied of dead entries with `list --prune` (entries of unknown liveness are kept and shown).
+- `fgos identity session --drop-role lead:<LANE>` removes that role from the calling session only, so a lead can give a lane up without ending its session: `resolve lead:<LANE>` is `not-found` afterwards, dropping a role the session does not hold exits 65 with `role-not-held`, and a session can never drop another session's role.
+- Every `fgos identity` refusal under `--json` now also prints one line of JSON on stdout, `{"error": <message>, "reason": <code>, "candidates": [...]}` (the sessions a `not-found` resolve was close to, the sessions an `ambiguous` name matches, each `{id, handle, liveness}`), so an agent reads the reason instead of parsing stderr. The exit code (65) and the stderr text are unchanged, and it is not a `fgos.v1` success envelope.
+- `fgos identity mint <kind> [--json]` is the one door for every id that travels between machines: `work` (`tsk-<10 base32>`) and `backlog` (`p-<10 base32>`) are random, `d-adr` (`D-ADR####`) and `decision-file` (`####`) are the next number of a counter ref `refs/fgos/seq/<kind>` on the project's `origin`, claimed with a compare-and-swap push so two machines never get the same number; `--release <number>` gives one back. New work items from `fgos add`, `fgos submit` and the runner's discovered work get ids from it (existing ids do not change), the merge-time decision renumbering is gone, doctor check `identity-ids-unique` fails on a repeated backlog id, `D-ADR` title clash or decision file number, and one always-loaded rule tells agents to take such ids from the verb. A claim needs the network and refuses clearly without it.
+- `fgos identity project --json` prints this project's id, handle and creation time, read from the tracked file `.fgos/project.json` of the main checkout, so every clone, machine and linked worktree prints the same id. Nothing mints it automatically: run `fgos identity project --init [--handle <name>]` once on one machine (it refuses when the file exists, in a linked worktree, or when the remote default branch already tracks it), commit the file with the printed command, and the other machines pull it; `--new` mints a different id on purpose to split a fork. `fgos doctor` has a new row `identity-project-id` that warns while the repository has none; it has no fix.
+- `fgos doctor` check `process-containment` now names why bwrap was not selected on Linux (including a refused host mount, which advises unmounting or fixing the mount rather than generic user-namespace advice), and the containment guarantee carries `selectedBecause`.
+- `fgos identity machine --json` prints this machine's id, its handle (`fg-server`, from the id without its suffix, or an alias) and its alias; `fgos identity machine --alias <name>` sets the alias (the handle changes, the id never does). The machine id is now minted and read by the Identity component, and Event Store reads it through that crate. `fgos doctor` has a new row `identity-machine-id`: it warns while no id exists and `fgos doctor --fix` mints it once. `fgos identity session --json` prints this session's full id (`<machine-id>/<local id>`) and a handle that never changes for the same session (`claude-4f2a@fg-server`), so an agent can paste it on the board; it exits 65 for a caller that cannot be told from any other. Bare `fgos identity` (also `fgos identity writer`) keeps `{id, source}` and adds optional `machine` and `session` parts, `null` when unknown; it never writes and never fails on a missing machine id.
+- `fgos run "<prompt>" --capability <cap>` and `--persona <name>` are no longer refused with `tier-escalation-unauthorized` when the capability's or persona's committed tier is above the default one (for example `--capability docs:write` with a flagship tier): they are the unit's own declarations, like the same keys of a `--unit` file. `--tier` and `--override` raises are still refused.
+- A herdr pane run no longer dies when the user's shell shows a start prompt (the oh-my-zsh update question) or agy shows its start banner: the launcher is typed only after the pane's shell has run a command and holds the foreground, panes start with `DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true` (it reaches the pane's process tree), and the banner is dismissed before the brief is typed. A launch can take up to 10 s longer when the shell is slow to answer, and the probe lines (up to 3) stay visible in a retained pane.
+- The writer identity now resolves inside the Node process through the native addon, so the first read costs about 40 microseconds instead of one `fgos identity` process (about 1.4 ms), later reads hit a small per-process cache, and a lock holder never waits on it. `fgos identity` stays for people, the git hook and `fgos doctor`; the host route `fgos internal identity mint-attempt` is removed, and the error codes `timeout`, `bad-output` and `identity-in-lock` are gone (`host-error` remains for the doctor probe).
+- Git remotes: an scp-form origin (`git@github.com:org/repo.git`) and an `ssh://user@host/...` origin now work for id minting (`fgos identity mint`), the Remote port and Event Store publication; one door reads the configured URL and refuses a host, user or path that could pass for an option, a git transport helper (`ext::`) or several arguments. A pinned URL now keeps a password-free ssh user name, so a stored pin recorded as `ssh://[redacted]@...` (only for ssh origins with a user, which Publication already refused) answers `remote URL changed; rerun setup` once: run `fgos setup` to re-record it. An origin of an unsupported transport (or one that cannot be read) now refuses an id claim and a give-back by name instead of using a local counter, and a remote URL with a query, a fragment, `::`, whitespace or control characters, or a user or host that starts with `-`, is refused by name.
+- A confined worker's herdr session socket is removed only when the OS refuses a connect twice on the same socket file; when the server's state cannot be judged (the route failed, a connect worked) the socket is kept and the dispatch fails with `worker-session-server-unknown` instead of starting a second server.
+- Git writes that fgOS reports as durable now stay durable under a repository or global `core.fsyncMethod=writeout-only`: every Git child fgOS runs with `core.fsync=all` also forces `core.fsyncMethod=fsync`, and a local id claim (`fgos identity mint` without an `origin`) is flushed to disk before its number is reported. A push the remote refuses for its own reason (a hook, a policy) reports that reason instead of a lost lease, a recovered repository-config change is acknowledged only after its file and directory are synced, and leftover temporary files of a failed journal write no longer count against the journal's size bound.
+- Git operations name their failures the same way in every port: a busy journal, a reused operation id, a changed repository identity and an unavailable publication borrow answer `refused` with a named cause, and a corrupt or unwritable journal answers `recovery-required` with the journal's own text under `detail.diagnostic`; a borrowed Git run that times out says `git-timeout` and one that overruns its output says `git-output-limit`, as a contained run does; a publication read of a shallow repository names `shallow-history-incomplete`; a dangling symbolic ref reads as symbolic, not absent; a remote or mapping name longer than 80 bytes is refused.

+- Admitting a lock over a dead predecessor whose process group or tree has a member that cannot die quickly now hands over or refuses within the 2000 ms kill wait. The kill used to wait up to 5 s for the domain to empty and only then start the 2000 ms, so a member stuck in uninterruptible I/O delayed the next holder by about 7 s.
+- A lock released while another thread of the same process forks children is now free to an immediate exclusive try: the release probe and `probe` unlock their private description before closing it, so a child forked in that window no longer keeps a shared lock and makes the next acquire answer `Held`.
+- A hot-mutex timeout whose record names a live holder that cannot be judged here now says `lock-record-unreadable` and names `fgos lock fence <resource>`, as for a record that does not parse, instead of advising to retry. On Windows a record another process holds open is waited on to the timeout and named, `fgos lock fence` and the doctor row report it, and a release whose unlink stays blocked throws `hot-lock-release-stuck` and leaves the record.
+- A durable write with a missing or out-of-range mode is refused by name (`durable-file-mode-invalid`, nothing installed) instead of failing inside the native layer.
+- `canonicalJson` now serialises as `JSON.stringify` does before canonicalising: a `Date` or any `toJSON` object becomes its `toJSON` text and a `Buffer` is accepted as `{type, data}`; a hole, an undefined array member, a non-finite number, a bigint and a function are still refused. Stored digests are unchanged.
+- A containment spawn that ends before reporting its gate pid now carries bwrap's own refusal line (for example the mount it could not remount) in the error text.
+- Node lock operations no longer start a helper process on Linux and macOS: acquiring, trying, waiting, probing, listing holders, draining a borrowed child and clearing a domain run in the Node process through the native addon, so an uncontended acquire takes microseconds instead of a host start. Releasing a lock now also ends any copy of it that escaped to a process the lock was not handed to, and `lock-holders` and `fgos lock-status` name each holder's origin as the host decides it. Windows keeps its `lock-hold` helper. The git pre-commit hook now asks the activated host (`fgos internal lock-fd --shared-try` for the lock, `fgos identity` for the writer) instead of loading the lock code from the checkout, and with no usable host the hook refuses at the writer-identity step instead of at the lock step.

+- Removed the config key `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` and the doctor row `lock-predecessor-kill-wait`: the predecessor kill wait is 2000 ms everywhere, as the Rust callers always had it. `fgos setup` no longer adds the `lock` section; an existing one is left alone and ignored.
+- Removed the `fgos doctor` rows `lock-record-unreadable` and `state-root`: the `state` and `porting-events` hot-record conditions now warn from `lock-holders`, and `lock-kernel-semantics` prints the state root with its source (and the fixed 2000 ms kill wait) and fails by name when it cannot be resolved. +- A run no longer stops with `terminal:foreground-not-agent` while its agent is working: a zombie child in the pane's foreground (herdr lists it without a command line) used to make the whole foreground unreadable, so the brief was refused. Zombies are now left out of the foreground.

+- Process identity (`src/runner/dispatch/process-identity.mjs`) now judges, observes and signals through the Rust process-facts crate by way of one in-process native door (`src/native/door.mjs`, the same addon Git loads), not through Node's own `/proc` reads. +- `fgos gateway stop` and `fgos lock fence` signal only the process whose recorded identity (pid, start time, boot) still matches, and refuse by name otherwise: a gateway registry entry written without an identity (an older entry) is refused as `gateway-stop-identity-unknown` / `gateway-start-identity-unknown` with the file to delete, `gateway status` reports it as `identity: unknown`, and a registry entry is cleared only once the process is proven gone. +- `fgos doctor` row `git-land-recovery` now also warns about finished Land operations whose candidate worktree and pins are still retained (operation id, candidate path, pins, age), and says there is no manual release command yet; the release sweep waits for the Work lane. Read-only, no cleanup.
+- A scoped runner commit now fsyncs the staged blobs and trees (file, fan-out directory and `objects/`) before `git commit` moves the branch, and the commit object before the receipt: before, the staged files and the directory entries were never fsynced, so a power cut could leave the branch naming a commit with an empty or missing tree or blob, acknowledged or not. Publication and scoped commits share one loose-object durability step. The E1 power-cut script gains `--kind scoped` for the same check.
+- A scoped runner commit no longer lets a power cut leave an empty blob or tree under its final object name: `git add` and `write-tree` now run with `core.fsync=loose-object` (each loose file is fsynced before Git links it). +- A project config that still carries `runner.rigorToTier` is refused by config validation, which names the key; delete it and declare `tier` per capability, role, persona or seat. `fgos setup` no longer converts a pre-seat config (it copies no `config.json.pre-seat-binding-*` backup and prints no conversion diff), and a project config with no `runner.patterns.seatBinding.schema` is no longer refused. +- `fgos doctor` no longer has the rows `runner-rigor-config` and `capability-rigor-ceiling` (rigor no longer maps to a tier or a ceiling); `model-policy-tier-coverage` and `workflow-pools-satisfy-independence` are replaced by `seat-binding-dry-bind`. +- A seat's account is named by the same decision as its executor and model: the lease takes exactly that account, a lease that cannot take it settles as `provider-capacity-lease-conflict` and the seat is bound again under the same policy, and a lease receipt the provider record does not back refuses a pass before anything is committed (`lease-receipt-mismatch`). An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Left as is, a future Agent Context Engine would be built beside `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs`, giving two composers and two orderings of the same rules. Owner decision: composing and selecting rules (kind order, override, conflict, per-task selection, per-host budget, progressive disclosure) has one owner, the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution keeps delivery (source discovery and install, per-host render adapters, projection ledger, doctor repair).
